An & that would read as a character reference in a link destination or title stays literal

```zig title="Zig"
const std = @import("std");
const html_to_markdown_rs = @import("html_to_markdown_rs");

pub fn main() !void {
    const _result_json = try html_to_markdown_rs.convert("<a href=\"?&amp;plus;\" title=\"&amp;plus;\">T</a>", null);
    defer std.heap.c_allocator.free(_result_json);
    std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{_result_json});

}
```
